2026-11-05.headline: Teams will organize muted and meeting chats into dedicated sections in January
2026-11-05.overview: Microsoft Teams will introduce a January 2027 chat reorganization: the Muted chats section will be enabled by default, while Meeting chats will be disabled by default, with users able to toggle and reorder both. Two worldwide changes are also planned for December 2026: a Workflows template that links team tags to channel membership and mobile call declines with chat messages. Documentation updates add certified-device entries and SlimCore troubleshooting detail.
2026-11-05.adminImpact: No required tenant-wide action is stated for the chat sections or mobile call-message feature. The Workflows template is optional and does not change defaults. Administrators should review the updated certified-hardware table during inventory and deployment planning; VDI support teams can use the specified BITS Client and AppXDeployment-Server logs when investigating SlimCore error 6/51.

keyChanges.title: Muted and meeting chats get dedicated sections in January 2027
keyChanges.detail: Teams will add Muted chats and Meeting chats sections. Muted chats will be enabled by default, while Meeting chats will be disabled by default. Users can enable or disable and reorder the sections, and muted chats move automatically unless they are favorited. Rollout begins in January 2027, with no admin action required.

keyChanges.title: Workflows will connect team tags to channel membership
keyChanges.detail: An optional Workflows app template will automatically add users to channels when they are added to a team tag. The feature rolls out worldwide in mid-December 2026 and does not change defaults.

keyChanges.title: Teams mobile users will be able to decline calls with messages
keyChanges.detail: Users will be able to decline incoming Teams mobile calls with a predefined or custom message sent through Teams chat. Worldwide rollout is scheduled for December 2026; the feature applies only to Teams-to-Teams calls with available chat and requires no admin action.

keyChanges.title: Certified Hardware Android adds Meeting Owl and Cisco entries
keyChanges.detail: The table now includes Meeting Owl 5 Pro, Owl Tablet, and multiple Cisco devices, along with their associated software versions and certification dates. Administrators can use these details when validating inventories and planning deployments.

keyChanges.title: SlimCore troubleshooting adds Windows error 6/51 guidance
keyChanges.detail: Vdi 2 Troubleshooting now documents Windows error 6/51, ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE, during SlimCore download, deployment, or startup, and points administrators to BITS Client and AppXDeployment-Server logs.

2026-11-06.headline: Teams Rooms app update tool is no longer recommended for new Autopilot deployments
2026-11-06.overview: This was a quiet, documentation-led day with one actionable Teams Rooms change. The Autopilot guidance says the Teams Rooms app has included automatic updates since April 2024, so the app update tool is no longer recommended for new deployments. A separate known-issues entry records possible Large Gallery unavailability on specified Teams Rooms for Android versions, while release notes document a low-bitrate video fix. Teams Phone updates only reorder language entries in reference and setup material.
2026-11-06.adminImpact: Review Intune assignments for the app update tool and consider unassigning it for new deployments, except when deploying devices older than 2025. Administrators should expect possible Large Gallery unavailability on the affected Android app versions; no action is specified for that issue or the low-bitrate video fix. The Teams Phone language-order changes require no configuration change.

keyChanges.title: Autopilot guidance changes the app update tool recommendation
keyChanges.detail: Because the Teams Rooms app has included automatic updates since April 2024, the app update tool is no longer recommended for new deployments. Administrators should review Intune configurations and consider unassigning the tool, except when deploying devices older than 2025.

keyChanges.title: Large Gallery may be unavailable on specified Teams Rooms for Android versions
keyChanges.detail: The known-issues page identifies possible Large Gallery unavailability on Teams Rooms for Android app versions 1449/1.0.96.2026249711 through 1449/1.0.96.2026264504. The issue is expected to be addressed in a future update, and no administrator action is specified.

keyChanges.title: Release notes record a low-bitrate video fix
keyChanges.detail: Teams Rooms release notes now document a fix for certain devices sending low-bitrate video in specific meeting scenarios. The supplied evidence states no administrator action.

2026-11-07.headline: Teams guidance shifts from webinar and town hall names to audience-based event labels
2026-11-07.overview: The period is dominated by terminology and procedure updates rather than product rollouts. Updated event guidance now uses “Events up to 1k attendees” and “Events optimized for a large audience” across recording, attendance, setup, captions, publishing, and chat topics. A separate Teams Rooms update revises screenshots and the note-saving workflow.
2026-11-07.adminImpact: Update administrator runbooks, training, and troubleshooting references to the audience-based event labels and the renamed “Events registration form questions” setting. The setup guidance says associated policy names and commands remain the same, transcription settings remain On by default, and the Teams Rooms update states that no administrator configuration change is required.

keyChanges.title: Policy references adopt audience-based event labels
keyChanges.detail: The Settings Policies Reference now uses “Events up to 1k attendees” and “Events optimized for a large audience” instead of webinar and town hall terminology across related settings. Use the revised labels when locating policy controls.

keyChanges.title: Recording guidance documents separate audience-size event settings
keyChanges.detail: The Meeting Recording article now groups webinars and town halls under events and documents settings for events with up to 1,000 attendees or for large audiences. It also clarifies policy-assignment instructions.

keyChanges.title: Anonymous-attendance instructions use the new event names
keyChanges.detail: The guide replaces “Who can attend webinars” and “Who can attend town halls” with “Who can attend events up to 1k attendees” and “Who can attend events optimized for a large audience,” and updates the configuration steps for anonymous participants.

keyChanges.title: Event registration setting receives a new documented name
keyChanges.detail: The setting formerly documented as “Webinar registration form questions” is now called “Events registration form questions.” Administrators should update internal configuration references and runbooks that use the previous name.

keyChanges.title: Teams Rooms note-saving workflow and visuals are revised
keyChanges.detail: The Facilitator Teams Rooms article updates screenshots, preview wording, and instructions for adding participant names when saving notes so participants can access notes and transcripts later. The revised workflow is useful for user guidance, with no administrator configuration change stated.

2026-11-09.headline: SIP Gateway plan drops Edge V 200+ firmware 8.5.1.0565 listing
2026-11-09.overview: The Devices update removes the Edge V 200+ entry with firmware version 8.5.1.0565 from the SIP Gateway plan’s IP Phone section.
2026-11-09.adminImpact: Administrators validating device and firmware support should review the updated SIP Gateway plan.

keyChanges.title: Edge V 200+ entry removed from the SIP Gateway plan
keyChanges.detail: The plan page no longer lists Edge V 200+ with firmware version 8.5.1.0565 under IP Phone. Use the revised plan when checking device and firmware support.

2026-11-10.headline: Teams Free off-network invitations retire as OneDrive video sharing reaches Teams events
2026-11-10.overview: The period brings a December 2026 retirement for off-network invitations to Teams Free, alongside mid-November rollouts for direct OneDrive video sharing in Teams events and policy-aligned recording controls. Teams also adds malicious QR-code detection through existing Malicious URL protection. The remaining updates are mainly Teams Rooms reference and hardware documentation changes.
2026-11-10.adminImpact: Update user guidance for Teams Free invitations before December 2026; existing Teams Free collaboration and federation remain unchanged. No administrator action is required for the OneDrive video-sharing, recording-policy, or QR-code protections, although administrators should verify that existing Malicious URL protection is enabled and should use the revised Teams Rooms hardware and PTZ references when evaluating devices.

keyChanges.title: Off-network invitations to Teams Free will be retired
keyChanges.detail: Starting in December 2026, users will no longer be able to invite external people by email or chat links to create Teams Free accounts. Existing Teams Free collaboration and federation remain unchanged, but user-facing guidance should be updated.

keyChanges.title: Teams events will support direct OneDrive video sharing
keyChanges.detail: Beginning in mid-November 2026, event organizers and producers can share OneDrive videos through “Manage what attendees see,” enabling playback without screen sharing or embedding the video in PowerPoint. No administrator action is required.

keyChanges.title: Meeting recording controls will reflect assigned policies
keyChanges.detail: From mid-November through mid-December 2026, meeting options will show automatic recording and transcription choices allowed by the organizer’s assigned policies, including a new “Record only” option.

keyChanges.title: Teams will detect malicious QR codes in chats and channels
keyChanges.detail: Starting in mid-November 2026, Teams will warn about harmful QR-code links, with external QR codes blurred by default. The capability is enabled through existing Malicious URL protection and requires no separate administrator action.

keyChanges.title: Teams Rooms references add PTZ support and a certified room kit
keyChanges.detail: The Teams Devices Feature Comparison now marks local pan-tilt-zoom controls as available in three rows, while the certified hardware list adds the AVer CORE500 Room Kit with a Core Ultra 5 processor, 16 GB of memory, and 256 GB of storage. These updates support device evaluation rather than signaling a new Teams Rooms rollout.

2026-11-11.headline: PMP requires Admin Agent 901 update as TAC device management deprecation approaches
2026-11-11.overview: Most of the 18 entries are documentation maintenance, but several carry direct operational weight. Admin Agent 901 adds Android 15 connectivity and provisioning fixes, cannot be paused, and is required for PMP device management. Teams Phone guidance documents authorized-user active-call controls and updated recording disclosures, while VDI HID guidance tightens version and architecture prerequisites. Teams Rooms guidance also sets a January 2027 retirement for M365 Targeted Release.
2026-11-11.adminImpact: Prioritize planning for the unpausable Admin Agent update and the planned TAC device-management deprecation. Review Teams Phone authorization, recording disclosures, and transcription handling; validate VDI Teams versions and MSIX architectures; and account for the January 2027 Teams Rooms release-channel change. Other updates are mainly reference, table, or troubleshooting maintenance.

keyChanges.title: Admin Agent 901 adds Android 15 fixes and is required for PMP management
keyChanges.detail: Certified Device Apps identifies version 1.0.0.202610190119 (Admin Agent 901) as adding critical Android 15 connectivity and provisioning fixes. The release is being accelerated across all Teams-certified devices, cannot be paused, is required to manage devices in PMP, and prepares for TAC device-management deprecation targeted for mid-November 2026.

keyChanges.title: Call-queue guidance documents four authorized-user active-call controls
keyChanges.detail: The Teams Phone call-queue cmdlet guidance states, effective November 10, 2026, that authorized users can join active calls through Monitor, Whisper, Barge, and Takeover.

keyChanges.title: Teams Phone Agent greeting explains recording and transcription handling
keyChanges.detail: The setup guidance changes the greeting to tell callers that calls are recorded. It states that calls are recorded and transcribed for service quality, inaccessible to humans, and deleted after processing; configured automatic recording greetings are used instead.

keyChanges.title: VDI HID guidance sets Teams version and client architecture prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: HID now requires Teams 26276.x.x.x or later. Citrix Workspace supports x86 or x64 MSIX packages, while Windows App and Horizon clients are 64-bit only; the previous HID Public Preview note was removed.

keyChanges.title: Teams Rooms guidance sets January 2027 retirement for M365 Targeted Release
keyChanges.detail: The Mtr Home Refresh page now references Microsoft Frontier and states that M365 Targeted Release is retiring in January 2027.

2026-11-02.headline: Teams will add muted and meeting chat sections in January 2027
2026-11-02.overview: Teams’ most consequential update this week is a planned January 2027 chat reorganization: users will get separate Muted chats and Meeting chats sections. The period also brings an optional tag-driven channel workflow, a broad shift in event-policy terminology, and two Teams Rooms administration issues: the app update tool is no longer recommended for new deployments, and Large Gallery may be unavailable on a defined Android app range.
2026-11-02.adminImpact: Chat sections require no admin action. The tag workflow is optional and does not change defaults, so admins can assess it for location- or project-based groups rather than prepare a tenant-wide change. For Teams Rooms, review Intune assignments for the app update tool: the guidance says automatic app updates have been included since April 2024 and suggests considering unassignment except for devices older than 2025. Update event runbooks and policy references to the labels “Events up to 1k attendees” and “Events optimized for a large audience.” On affected Android Rooms versions, expect Large Gallery to be unavailable.

keyChanges.title: New sections will organize muted and meeting chats
keyChanges.detail: Teams will introduce Muted chats, enabled by default, and Meeting chats, disabled by default, beginning in January 2027. Users can enable, disable, and reorder the sections; muted chats move automatically into their section unless they are favorited.

keyChanges.title: A Workflows template will sync team tags with channels
keyChanges.detail: An optional Workflows app template will automatically add users to channels when they are added to a team tag. Worldwide rollout is scheduled for mid-December 2026, with no default changes, supporting location- or project-based groups.

keyChanges.title: Event policy references now use attendee-capacity labels
keyChanges.detail: The Settings Policies Reference now uses “Events up to 1k attendees” and “Events optimized for a large audience” instead of webinar and town hall terminology across related settings.

keyChanges.title: Teams Rooms guidance no longer recommends the app update tool for new deployments
keyChanges.detail: The Autopilot Autologin guidance says Teams Rooms app automatic updates have been included since April 2024, so the app update tool is no longer recommended for new deployments. It advises reviewing Intune assignments and considering unassignment except when deploying devices older than 2025.

keyChanges.title: Large Gallery may be unavailable on specific Android Rooms builds
keyChanges.detail: The known-issues page identifies a limitation on Teams Rooms for Android app versions 1449/1.0.96.2026249711 through 1449/1.0.96.2026264504. Administrators should expect Large Gallery to be unavailable on those builds while awaiting a future update.

2026-11-09.headline: Teams events gain direct OneDrive video sharing in November rollout
2026-11-09.overview: Teams’ most consequential changes this week are a mid-November event workflow that lets organizers and producers share OneDrive videos through “Manage what attendees see,” alongside policy-filtered recording controls and malicious QR-code detection. A separate December retirement will stop off-network invitations from creating Teams Free accounts, while Teams-certified device management is moving toward PMP and away from TAC. Most remaining updates were reference maintenance, although Teams Phone guidance repeatedly documents authorized users joining active calls through Monitor, Whisper, Barge, and Takeover.
2026-11-09.adminImpact: Update user guidance before the December Teams Free invitation change. For Teams-certified Android devices, Admin Agent version 1.0.0.202610190119 cannot be paused and is required for PMP management; administrators should prepare for TAC device-management deprecation targeted for mid-November 2026. The other highlighted rollouts state that no special admin action is required, with recording options constrained by assigned policies and QR protection using existing Malicious URL protection.

keyChanges.title: OneDrive videos become a direct sharing source for Teams events
keyChanges.detail: Starting in mid-November 2026, event organizers and producers can share videos directly from OneDrive through “Manage what attendees see,” avoiding screen sharing or PowerPoint embedding and enabling higher-quality playback. No admin action is required.

keyChanges.title: Off-network invitations to Teams Free retire in December
keyChanges.detail: Starting in December 2026, users can no longer invite external people by email or chat link to create Teams Free accounts. Existing Teams Free collaboration and federation remain unchanged; Microsoft says administrators should update user guidance.

keyChanges.title: Meeting recording choices will reflect assigned admin policies
keyChanges.detail: From mid-November through mid-December 2026, meeting options will show automatic recording and transcription settings permitted by assigned policies, including a new “Record only” option. Organizers will see only policy-allowed choices, with no admin action required.

keyChanges.title: Teams adds malicious QR-code detection to chats and channels
keyChanges.detail: Beginning in mid-November 2026, Teams will detect malicious QR codes in chats and channels and blur external QR codes by default. The protection uses existing Malicious URL protection and requires no admin action.

keyChanges.title: Admin Agent 901 brings PMP fixes ahead of TAC management deprecation
keyChanges.detail: The Certified Device Apps entry identifies version 1.0.0.202610190119 (Admin Agent 901) as adding Android 15 connectivity and provisioning fixes for PMP and being accelerated across Teams-certified devices. The update cannot be paused and is required for PMP management; TAC device-management deprecation is targeted for mid-November 2026.

2026-11.headline: Teams events gain OneDrive video sharing as policy controls and security rollouts expand
2026-11.overview: November’s strongest changes are operational: Teams events are gaining direct OneDrive video sharing, meeting recording and transcription options will reflect assigned policies, and off-network invitations to Teams Free will retire in December. Malicious QR-code detection is also rolling out in chats and channels through existing Malicious URL protection. For Teams-certified Android devices, an unpausable Admin Agent update is required for Pro Management Portal management as Microsoft prepares to deprecate TAC device management. Much of the remaining activity standardizes event terminology and refreshes deployment and troubleshooting guidance.
2026-11.adminImpact: Update user guidance for the December Teams Free invitation retirement. No special administrator action is stated for OneDrive video sharing, policy-aligned recording options, or QR-code detection; organizers will see only recording settings allowed by their policies, and QR protection uses existing Malicious URL protection. For certified Android devices, account for the required Admin Agent update and prepare for the planned TAC device-management deprecation. Event runbooks should adopt the capability-based labels “Events up to 1k attendees” and “Events optimized for a large audience” where applicable.

keyChanges.title: Organizers can share OneDrive videos directly in Teams events
keyChanges.detail: Beginning in mid-November 2026, event organizers and producers can use “Manage what attendees see” to share videos from OneDrive, avoiding screen sharing or PowerPoint embedding and enabling smoother, higher-quality playback. No administrator action is required.

keyChanges.title: Meeting options align recording controls with assigned policies
keyChanges.detail: Rolling out from mid-November through mid-December 2026, automatic recording and transcription options will reflect each organizer’s assigned policies. The update adds a “Record only” option, and organizers will see only settings their policies allow.

keyChanges.title: Off-network invitations to Teams Free retire in December
keyChanges.detail: Starting in December 2026, users will no longer be able to invite external people by email or chat link to create Teams Free accounts. Existing Teams Free collaboration and federation remain unchanged, but user guidance should be updated.

keyChanges.title: Teams adds malicious QR-code detection to messages
keyChanges.detail: From mid-November 2026, Teams will detect potentially malicious QR codes in chats and channels, warn users about harmful links, and blur external QR codes by default. The capability is enabled through existing Malicious URL protection and requires no administrator action.

keyChanges.title: A required Android agent update accelerates the move to PMP
keyChanges.detail: Certified Teams Android devices are receiving version 1.0.0.202610190119 (Admin Agent 901), which adds Android 15 connectivity and provisioning fixes. The update cannot be paused and is required for device management in the Pro Management Portal; the documentation also prepares administrators for TAC device-management deprecation targeted for mid-November 2026.
